summary: ComfyUI-Easy-Use version 1.3.6 contains a path traversal vulnerability in the `save_preview()`...
description: ComfyUI-Easy-Use version 1.3.6 contains a path traversal vulnerability in the `save_preview()` handler for POST `/easyuse/save/{name}`. The handler checks the source directory before appending a user-supplied filename and allows the request to select the `custom_nodes` directory as a copy destination. An unauthenticated attacker who can reach the ComfyUI server can overwrite an installed custom node’s Python entry point with an uploaded file. When ComfyUI restarts and loads the modified node, the attacker’s code runs with the privileges of the ComfyUI process.

summary: Out-of-bounds Read vulnerability in the Guththila XML parser wrapper of Apache Axis2/C. On some...
description: Out-of-bounds Read vulnerability in the Guththila XML parser wrapper of Apache Axis2/C. On some malformed XML input the Guththila parser returned a raw input byte in place of an event code, and the AXIOM reader wrapper used that value as an index into a ten-entry lookup table without checking its range, reading heap memory past the end of the table. An unauthenticated client could trigger this by sending a crafted XML request to a server built with Guththila, the default parser, causing the request to be parsed incorrectly or, in some cases, the process to crash. The memory read is not returned to the client. This issue affects Apache Axis2/C: through 2.0.0. The fix is available in commits 23110287924e79d05a5b4712298c355d1f05c606 and f01683ec10e8fddb87279ec9351b3239021223e6 and will be included in the next release.

description: When a remote, unauthenticated HTTP/1.1 client pipelined the start of a second request and then stopped reading, proxygen's coroutine-based HTTP session could free that pipelined stream while resetting the connection's streams on the resulting write timeout, then go on to use it. summary: proxygen's HTTP/3 codec buffered an incomplete non-DATA frame, such as a control-stream frame, a...
description: proxygen's HTTP/3 codec buffered an incomplete non-DATA frame, such as a control-stream frame, a frame of an unknown or reserved type, or a HEADERS frame, until its entire declared length had arrived, without limiting that length, and re-scanned all buffered data each time more bytes arrived. A remote, unauthenticated HTTP/3 peer could declare a very large frame and deliver it slowly, causing unbounded memory growth and CPU usage that grows quadratically with the number of fragments, leading to denial of service. summary: An mvfst QUIC server retained CRYPTO frame data received at an encryption level (Initial or...
description: An mvfst QUIC server retained CRYPTO frame data received at an encryption level (Initial or Handshake) that the TLS handshake had already moved past. Because the transport treated this data as delivered, it did not count against the CRYPTO stream buffer limit. A remote, unauthenticated client could complete a handshake, withhold its acknowledgment of the server's HANDSHAKE_DONE frame so that Handshake keys stay in use, and keep sending Handshake-level CRYPTO data at increasing offsets, causing unbounded memory growth on the server and leading to denial of service. This issue affects mvfst versions prior to v2026.11.09.00.

summary: proxygen's QPACK decoder enforced its size limit on a string literal in an encoder-stream...
description: proxygen's QPACK decoder enforced its size limit on a string literal in an encoder-stream instruction only after the entire literal had been received. A remote, unauthenticated HTTP/3 peer could send an insert instruction on the QPACK encoder stream that declares an arbitrarily large literal and then keep sending data, causing the decoder to buffer it without bound for the lifetime of the connection and exhaust memory, leading to denial of service. The issue occurs regardless of the advertised QPACK dynamic table capacity, including when the dynamic table is disabled. This issue affects proxygen versions prior to v2026.11.09.00.

summary: In proxygen's HTTP/3 session, when a HEADERS block referenced QPACK dynamic table entries that...
description: In proxygen's HTTP/3 session, when a HEADERS block referenced QPACK dynamic table entries that had not yet been received, header decoding for that stream was paused, but the session continued to read the stream from the QUIC transport. The unread data bypassed the session's ingress buffer limit, returned flow-control credit to the peer, and was re-scanned in full on every read. With QPACK blocked streams enabled (the default), a remote, unauthenticated HTTP/3 peer could send a HEADERS block that references a dynamic table insert it never sends, followed by a continuous stream of data, causing memory growth until the request timed out and CPU usage that grows quadratically, leading to denial of service. This issue affects proxygen versions prior to v2026.11.09.00.

summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

inet: reject unhashed...
description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

inet: reject unhashed sockets during established lookups

TCP established ehash lookups are lockless. The socket caches involved
use SLAB_TYPESAFE_BY_RCU, so memory can be reused before an RCU reader
that retained its old address has finished.

After a tuple match, __inet_lookup_established() and
__inet6_lookup_established() acquire a reference and repeat the tuple
check. They do not check whether the new object is hashed. If the
address is reused for a socket with the same tuple, the lookup can
acquire a reference to the new object and return it while its nulls node
is unhashed.

A PoC that drives reuse with a SYN cookie request socket reproduced the
crash. The new request socket is unhashed and has a NULL rsk_listener.
A lookup that had loaded the address of the old request socket acquired
the reference published by tcp_get_cookie_sock() and returned the new
object. tcp_v4_rcv() then read sk_state through the NULL listener.

The resulting crash was:

  BUG: kernel NULL pointer dereference, address: 0000000000000012
  #PF: supervisor read access in kernel mode
  #PF: error_code(0x0000) - not-present page
  ...
  Oops: Oops: 0000 [#1] SMP NOPTI
  CPU: 4 UID: 0 PID: 0 Comm: swapper/4 Not tainted 7.3.0-00591-g0e135910deec #1 PREEMPT(lazy)
  ...
  RIP: 0010:tcp_v4_rcv+0x44e/0x1280
  ...
  R10: 0000000000000001 R11: 00000000024ca8c0 R12: 0000000000000000
  ...
  CR2: 0000000000000012 CR3: 0000000103d50004 CR4: 0000000000770ef0
  ...
  Call Trace:
   <IRQ>
   ? raw_local_deliver+0xae/0x240
   ip_protocol_deliver_rcu+0x2d/0x180
   ip_local_deliver_finish+0x84/0x100
   ip_sublist_rcv_finish+0x5f/0x70
   ip_sublist_rcv+0x12a/0x1d0
   ip_list_rcv+0xfd/0x130
   __netif_receive_skb_list_core+0x223/0x250
   netif_receive_skb_list_internal+0x1d2/0x2c0
   ? try_fill_recv+0x39/0x7b0
   napi_complete_done+0x74/0x170
   virtnet_poll+0x445/0x600
   __napi_poll+0x27/0x1e0
   net_rx_action+0x2fe/0x3b0
   handle_softirqs+0xc2/0x2c0
   __irq_exit_rcu+0x74/0xd0
   common_interrupt+0x7f/0x90
   </IRQ>
  ...
  Kernel panic - not syncing: Fatal exception in interrupt

After taking a reference, check whether the nulls node is unhashed in
both IPv4 and IPv6 established lookups. If it is unhashed or the tuple
no longer matches, drop the reference and restart the lookup.

Lookups racing with the TIME_WAIT hashdance, or with a request being
replaced by its child, now restart and find the new socket instead of
returning the old one.

Request sockets that were never inserted into ehash can have a nonzero
refcount, and a stale lookup can hold a transient reference. Therefore,
when SYN cookie, Fast Open, and request migration paths fail after
setting a nonzero refcount, release the references held by those paths
with reqsk_put() instead of freeing the request directly.

Due to a Debian-specific patch, the directory used to share data between the
LightDM and the users logging in was writable by the lightdm user of the
unprivileged greeter process. A process running under the lightdm identity

(running as root) to change ownership and permissions on other root-owned
directories and escalate privileges from the lightdm user to root.

summary:
Issue summary: A QUIC server that rejects a stream opened by the peer may
retain that stream's...
description:
Issue summary: A QUIC server that rejects a stream opened by the peer may
retain that stream's state for the lifetime of the connection if the peer
resets the stream before the rejection is signalled, even though the peer's
stream credit is returned.

Impact summary: A remote client that completes a QUIC handshake can repeatedly
open and reset streams, causing server memory to grow without bound until the
process runs out of memory and every connection on it is lost. This is a
Denial of Service.

CWE: CWE-401: Missing Release of Memory after Effective Lifetime

Description: QUIC servers track each stream the peer opens. When the incoming
stream policy rejects a stream, OpenSSL schedules a STOP_SENDING frame, marks
the stream deleted and returns the peer's stream credit. A deleted stream is
collected only once its receive part is fully drained, which for a rejected
stream means the STOP_SENDING has been acknowledged. If the peer sends
RESET_STREAM first, the reset cancels the pending STOP_SENDING, so it is never
sent or acknowledged and the stream is never collected.

The default configuration reaches this path. Once a connection has a default
stream, meaning the application has read from or written to the connection as
the tutorial server does, the effective incoming stream policy rejects streams
the application does not accept. Applications that set the REJECT policy
explicitly are affected too.

Each retained stream costs about 300 bytes, and the peer's stream credit
window paces how quickly they accumulate. A client that keeps the connection
open and keeps opening and resetting streams grows server memory without
bound. The severity is Low because growth is slow, needs a long-lived
connection, and causes no memory corruption or disclosure.

FIPS impact: no
The affected code is outside the FIPS module boundary.

cwes.name: Missing Release of Memory after Effective Lifetime

summary: JSON::XS versions from 3.04 before 4.05 for Perl write one byte past a heap buffer when appending...
description:
JSON::XS versions from 3.04 before 4.05 for Perl write one byte past a heap buffer when appending a one-byte chunk in incr_parse.

The incremental buffer grows to one and a half times the length it must hold, with no room reserved for the terminating NUL. For an empty buffer and a one-byte chunk that request is one byte, which a buffer whose front was removed by earlier decodes can already have, so nothing is reallocated and the NUL lands one byte past the allocation.

A peer streaming data to an incr_parse consumer, choosing how the input is split into reads, can cause a one-byte heap out-of-bounds write.

summary: JSON::XS versions from 3.0 before 4.05 for Perl read freed stack memory when a FREEZE result's...
description:
JSON::XS versions from 3.0 before 4.05 for Perl read freed stack memory when a FREEZE result's serialisation grows the Perl stack under allow_tags in encode_rv.

With allow_tags, an object's FREEZE method is called in list context and each returned value is encoded through a saved Perl stack pointer. When encoding a returned value calls back into Perl, through TO_JSON under convert_blessed or another FREEZE, and that callback grows the stack, the stack is reallocated while the saved pointer still refers to the freed block.

Encoding such objects reads freed memory, and encode can return undef without an error.

summary: JSON::XS versions before 4.05 for Perl leak the decoded key of an object rejected for a missing...
description:
JSON::XS versions before 4.05 for Perl leak the decoded key of an object rejected for a missing colon in decode_hv.

Unless it is short plain ASCII, a quoted key is decoded into a new scalar. Nothing frees that scalar when the object is rejected for a missing ':' after the key.

A process that keeps running after a failed decode retains one key per rejected document, with its size chosen by the sender. Repeated requests exhaust process memory.

summary: JSON::XS versions before 4.05 for Perl allow memory exhaustion by buffering incremental input...
description:
JSON::XS versions before 4.05 for Perl allow memory exhaustion by buffering incremental input past max_size after a NUL byte in incr_parse.

The parser appends each chunk to its buffer and compares max_size with how far it has progressed, not with the buffer length. It treats a NUL byte as the end of the input, so a NUL within the first max_size bytes keeps it short of the limit. The buffer keeps growing, and incr_skip cannot remove the NUL.

A peer streaming data to an incr_parse consumer can exhaust process memory regardless of max_size.

summary: In Eclipse AAS4J before 3.0.1, `XmlSchemaValidator.validateSchema()` (and `AASXValidator...
description:
In Eclipse AAS4J before 3.0.1, `XmlSchemaValidator.validateSchema()` (and `AASXValidator.validateSchema()`, which calls it) validates untrusted XML with a default JAXP `Validator` that resolves external DTDs and external entities. An attacker who supplies a crafted AAS XML document or AASX package can read local files from the host, send their contents out-of-band to an attacker-controlled server, and make the validating process send arbitrary outbound requests (SSRF). Validation still returns no errors.



Details:



- Vulnerable code: `dataformat-xml/src/main/java/org/eclipse/digitaltwin/aas4j/v3/dataformat/xml/XmlSchemaValidator.java`. `schema.newValidator().validate(new StreamSource(...))` runs without `ACCESS_EXTERNAL_DTD` / `ACCESS_EXTERNAL_SCHEMA` restrictions and without `disallow-doctype-decl`.



- Second entry point: `dataformat-aasx/src/main/java/org/eclipse/digitaltwin/aas4j/v3/dataformat/aasx/AASXValidator.java`. The AAS XML part of an `.aasx` package is passed unchanged to the vulnerable validator.



- `XmlDeserializer` (Jackson/Woodstox) is not affected, because DTD support is disabled by default there.



- Present since the initial import of the code base (commit `cc9da52`).



- Fix: harden the validator by setting `ACCESS_EXTERNAL_DTD` and `ACCESS_EXTERNAL_SCHEMA` to `""` and rejecting `DOCTYPE` declarations. The bundled `AAS.xsd` does not need DTDs, so no functionality is lost.
